0.4.0 uses one H.264 viewer for Android emulators and iOS simulators. Android still uses scrcpy and the device encoder. iOS now uses the simulator helper's native H.264 encoder; the proxy converts AVCC records to Annex-B without decoding or re-encoding video on the host.

## Changed

- Video buffers stay bounded. After dropping dependent frames, playback waits for a keyframe rather than decoding an incomplete sequence.
- Decoder setup, playback, reset, and terminal disposal have explicit states. Obsolete codec checks and decoder outputs cannot revive a stopped viewer.
- Capture recovery keeps the device handle and automation session attached. If the capture helper exits, the next stream request restarts capture and rotates the viewer proxy's credentials.
- Device ownership records now include reservation, attachment, retirement, rollback, and failed cleanup. Failed cleanup keeps ownership reserved, and retries only unfinished steps.
- Cancelling queued work prevents dispatch. Cancelling running native commands terminates the command before the queue advances; input already sent to the device cannot be undone.
- Native operations have a 120-second deadline. The RPC deadline allows another 15 seconds for cancellation, cleanup, and returning an outcome. Failures retain whether the action may have executed.

## Fixed

- A capture helper that exits between readiness and publication is rejected instead of being returned as active.
- Failed initial state publication closes the desktop connection so a fresh connection can retry. Late readiness completion cannot resurrect a closed connection.
- Failed or ended session-event subscriptions reconnect with cancellable backoff, capped at five seconds.
- Cleanup after session deletion or movement remains retryable and does not block another session's cleanup.
- Shutdown intent survives failed cleanup. Physical-device aliases cannot bypass ownership or cause rollback to shut down another session's device.
- Disposal cancels pending discovery and recovery. Destroyed viewers cannot reconnect or retain decode timers.

Overlapping old tests were consolidated into transition tables, and the previous all-in-one desktop test was split into focused cases. Production function complexity is limited to nine. No runtime dependency or FSM framework was added.

## Update

Update the plugin pin in your global OpenCode configuration, preserving other settings:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["github:viralcodex/opencode-demul#v0.4.0"]
}
```

Plugin exports and tool names are unchanged. Android still requires SDK Platform-Tools, Emulator, and a configured AVD. iOS requires Xcode and an iOS Simulator runtime on macOS. Both require Node 22.19+ on the 22.x line, or Node 24+, with npm.

Validation includes lint, formatting, typechecking, 296 passing tests and one existing Bun-only skip, rebuilt bundles, and installed-package loading. Each implementation PR passed Linux CI before merging; lifecycle suites also passed three consecutive local runs. Two fresh helper installations, native module loading, offline reuse, and stale-cache rejection passed on macOS arm64.

Full changelog: https://github.com/viralcodex/opencode-demul/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0
